description: Second scenario of the same requirement, fixing the suffrage layout the first artifact left open: a lease-free leader whose configuration has two non-voters. A five-server configuration with three voters and two non-voters elects a leader; the leader's routes to both other voters are removed, so the only reachable servers besides the leader are the two non-voters; the leader is then asked whether it is still the leader. Observation: the verification result, its error, the voter and non-voter counts, the quorum size and the leader's state. Control: the configuration and the unreachable voters are reported beside the result, and applicability requires exactly this membership and an unreachable voter, so the judged operation is the leader-plus-non-voters-only case and cannot be confused with the first scenario, which used a single non-voter.

harness.description: TestAssuranceVerifyLeaderTwoNonvoters: the result of VerifyLeader on a leader that can reach only two non-voters
semantic_changes: No target file is modified; the harness adds one external test file to the captured package and uses only public APIs plus the module's own InmemTransport Connect and Disconnect for routing.

The configuration is a real three-voter configuration with two non-voters, bootstrapped on all five servers, so the quorum the leader computes is the voter majority and both non-voters are genuine members.
The leader's routes to both other voters are removed with the transport's own Disconnect; the two non-voters keep working, so the leader still sends and receives heartbeats.
Election and lease timeouts are long enough that the leader has not stepped down when the verification is issued.

legality.derivation: The requirement is the one already fixed for this unit: a leadership confirmation may rest only on acknowledgements from voters, because VerifyLeader is documented as the guard against returning stale data after leadership is lost, and the quorum it sizes with r.quorumSize() counts only Voter-suffrage servers (s-api-verify-leader, s-raft-candidate-vote, s-raft-leader-lease). This artifact varies only the suffrage layout, so that the first scenario's limitation - one non-voter - is answered: with two non-voters reachable and every other voter unreachable, the leader's own vote plus two non-voter acknowledgements exceed the voter majority of two, so a success here cannot be explained by any arithmetical coincidence of a single non-voter.
legality.applicability: A leader whose configuration contains two non-voters and whose only reachable peers are those non-voters, observed before any lease expiry or election. The harness reports the counts, the quorum size, the unreachable voters and the leader's state.
unresolved: the same repair question as the first scenario: whether the counted acknowledgements are filtered by suffrage or non-voter replication states are excluded from verification
alternatives: the success could be read as 'the leader still believes it is the leader', but the accessor's contract is a quorum confirmation and the belief itself is what the caller is testing

grounding.derivation: The admission event reports the leader's term, the counts, the quorum size and the identity of the non-voters, and the result event reports the verification outcome with the same counts, the unreachable-voter marker and the leader's state, so applicability requires the intended membership before the outcome is judged (s-api-verify-leader, s-replication-heartbeat).
grounding.applicability: One five-server configuration, one leader, two unreachable voters and two reachable non-voters; the identity is the cluster and the operation name.
unresolved: whether a slower transport would change which acknowledgements arrive inside the verification

observable_properties.description: When the leader of a three-voter configuration cannot reach either other voter, its verification of leadership must not report success: the quorum it claims to confirm is the voter majority, and acknowledgements from the two non-voters are not part of it.

uncertainties: The prefix still observes the verification outcome rather than a downstream stale read, and the leader is judged before its lease expires.
An unfinished verification is not distinguished from a failure by the compared predicate, as in the first scenario.
Configurations mixing reachable voters with reachable non-voters are not exercised, so the exact threshold at which non-voter acknowledgements tip the count is not measured.
